solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A butcher's working capital

indicators.note: working here means operating in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive's S is kept as a letter in the fodder

explanation.surface: A meat trader running his business on borrowed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in a butcher's working capital, but it is a capital city; 'working' rearranges A BUTCHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romanian capital city is a typical example of a national capital.

clue.text: You may follow it after involuntary expulsion!

definitions.text: You may follow it after involuntary expulsion!

parts.words: You may follow it after involuntary expulsion
parts.note: after a sneeze (an involuntary expulsion of air) someone says the word with 'you' after it

explanation.surface: A dark hint at being thrown out of somewhere against one's will.
explanation.walkthrough: The expulsion is a sneeze, not an eviction; the customary response is this word followed by 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The customary response to a sneeze is a blessing, the verb completed by the word you.

clue.text: Look! Drunken Ray can't see right away

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters of the three words are jumbled
away tells us the letter for right is removed

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is too drunk to see straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' shuffles RAY CANT SEE, and 'away' removes the R (for 'right'), leaving the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance over something is to give it a look, an idiom used as an imperative.

clue.text: Fortune people held in fiddling salt quotas

indicators.note: held in means the first pieces sit within the jumbled letters
fiddling suggests tampering, so the letters of salt are rearranged

parts.note: lot means one's fortune or fate
men is a common crossword synonym for people

explanation.surface: Some fortune-hunters cheating on rationed supplies of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fortune' reads as wealth, but here it is one's fate or portion; 'fiddling' scrambles salt to ALTS, which is split after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocated shares or portions handed out to each party are quotas.

clue.text: Replays in which opponents want hearts

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit as opponents, giving E and N
cores are the hearts or centres of things

explanation.surface: Card players hoping their rivals will lead hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and North are on opposite sides, so 'opponents' gives E and N; 'hearts' is not the card suit but centres.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra performances demanded by an audience are repeats of a piece, hence replays.

clue.text: Occupation found in centre of boisterous French city

indicators.note: centre of picks the two middle letters of the ten-letter word

parts.note: Nancy is a city in north-eastern France

explanation.surface: A rowdy part of a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupation of a property as a tenant, holding it for a term, is a synonym.

clue.text: Mob invading smashes war memorial

indicators.note: invading means the letters are found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A crowd storms in and wrecks a war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across smaSHES WAR Memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense crowd moving in a mass is a synonym for a mob.

clue.text: Become diamonds possibly

definitions.meaning: to become someone is to flatter or look right on them, as clothing does
diamonds is one of the four card categories, alongside clubs, hearts and spades

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to look good on someone and a set of playing cards.

clue.text: Quiet words spoken in a swindle, oddly

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word swindle

explanation.surface: Murmured remarks during a con trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of 'swindle' (S, I, D, E).
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made quietly, typically by an actor to the audience, is a stage whisper.

clue.text: Horse with rider joins as part of posse

parts.note: the rider is the man on horseback
a hunter is a horse bred for hunting

explanation.surface: A horseman signs up with a sheriff's band.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN joins HUNTER to make the whole; 'with' and 'joins' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group out pursuing a fugitive, so each member is a tracker of people.

clue.text: Support and comfort wanted by fifty

parts.note: ease means comfort
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A pensioner at fifty wanting backing and relaxation.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand for holding a canvas is a type of support.

clue.text: State qualification

definitions.meaning: a state of something is its shape or fitness
a qualification is a proviso or stipulation attached to an agreement

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's state of health and a stipulation that limits an agreement.

clue.text: Straighten out with devastating result

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word are put out of order

explanation.surface: Sorting out a problem with disastrous consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crushing or overwhelming in its effect is devastating, a close synonym.

clue.text: What Cupid has, say, for a sweetheart

indicators.note: say tells us to pronounce the word aloud

parts.note: Cupid carries a bow and arrows

explanation.surface: Cupid's equipment for a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Cupid's bow, said aloud, gives the French-derived word for a boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend or male admirer is an old-fashioned term for a sweetheart.

clue.text: There's the rub, seen also in 21

definitions.meaning: rubbing or chafing causes soreness, and a rub is an annoyance
the 21-down answer contains the word ITCH, which is a prickling annoyance

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cross-reference: the letters ITCH appear inside 21-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance or chafing soreness is the shared sense of both halves.

clue.text: Probes made by policemen once, loud not quiet

indicators.note: in music F (forte) is loud and P (piano) is quiet, so one letter replaces the other

parts.note: peelers was a nickname for early London police officers, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.surface: Former police officers investigating noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: Peelers were the first London police, named after Robert Peel who founded them.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae or tentative inquiries are probes into something.

clue.text: Bird that ploughmen have for lunch?

definitions.meaning: a thrush-like bird that visits Britain in winter
food eaten in the field by farm workers, read as a whimsical phrase

explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This winter thrush is a species of bird, and the name splits into a meal taken in the field.

clue.text: Rewrite history with king, not 21, opposing Lancaster

indicators.note: rewrite means the letters are written again in another order
not tells us the letter given by the cross-reference is removed

parts.note: 21-down spells out the name of the letter H
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Revising history in the time of a king who fought the house of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Wars of the Roses the house of York fought the house of Lancaster. Drop H from HISTORY, add K, then 'Rewrite' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the house of York was on the opposite side to Lancaster.

clue.text: Where outlaw hides in Albania (among other things)

definitions.meaning: the word ban (outlaw) sits between the letters AL and IA in Albania
a Latin phrase for including various other things

explanation.walkthrough: Outlaw as a verb is BAN, which is placed in among the letters of ALIA to make Albania.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase literally means among others and also describes BAN placed between A-L-I-A.

clue.text: I choose whether spades lead or not

definitions.text: I choose whether spades lead or not

parts.words: I choose whether spades lead or not
parts.note: a voter chooses; put S (spades) at the front and the word becomes another kind of chooser

explanation.surface: A card player deciding whether to lead a spade.
explanation.walkthrough: With S in front it becomes SELECTOR; with or without S, it is someone who chooses.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter is one who chooses, speaking here in the first person.

clue.text: Flute with note missing — requisition another!

indicators.note: missing means a letter is taken out

parts.note: a recorder is a kind of end-blown flute
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A broken flute with a note missing must be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a fresh order for supplies is to requisition again.

clue.text: Artist's bow tie

definitions.meaning: the 's stands for is, joining the two senses; an artist works in oils or watercolour
a rope at the bow of a boat used to tie it up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a person who makes pictures and a mooring rope at the front of a boat.

clue.text: Prisoner initially let out like Punch?

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of prisoner

parts.note: leased means rented or let out

explanation.surface: A prisoner first released, as happy as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pleased as Punch' is an English idiom, from the Punch and Judy puppet show.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pleased as Punch means delighted, so this is how Punch is.

clue.text: Rather dull old poet rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bard is an old word for a poet

explanation.surface: A tedious ancient poet who was turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary, colourless and lacking interest describes something rather dull.

clue.text: What's often omitted in speech

parts.note: many English accents drop the initial H sound from words like house

explanation.surface: Words left out when someone talks.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the name of the letter H, dropped by many British speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the letter that many accents drop from the start of words.

clue.text: Cart bearing single male requiring transplant tissue

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the cart holds the other letters

parts.note: a barrow is a small cart
one means single

explanation.surface: A single man needs carting off for a transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft tissue inside bones is what is transplanted in leukaemia treatment.

clue.text: Superlative? Paradoxically, it is!

parts.note: the word is a grammatical superlative, yet means the opposite of superlative in the sense of excellent

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that something is supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bad is a superlative form, though it denotes the least excellent.

clue.text: What boxers do at 28, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: 28-across means jobless or surplus, the same as spare

explanation.surface: Boxers' activity when idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers practise fighting with partners in training bouts.

clue.text: Does it pan out where diggers live?

indicators.note: pan out suggests working out a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gold prospector asks whether the panning will pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: Diggers is slang for Australians, not miners, despite the gold-panning picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia and New Zealand are on the opposite side of the globe from Britain.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing Reid plays outside left

indicators.note: outside means the anagram goes round the other letter
plays suggests the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A lazy footballer named Reid on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges REID as IDER, which goes 'outside' L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who avoids work is a layabout or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: A number of Soviet heroes

indicators.note: of signals the letters come from within the phrase

explanation.surface: Counting some Soviet war heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' means a thing that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An old anaesthetic numbs the patient, so it is a number in that sense.

clue.text: Socialist worker welcomes German and ends up jobless!

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the German word goes inside

parts.note: red is a common word for a socialist
an ant is a worker insect
und is German for and

explanation.surface: A left-wing worker who befriends a German is laid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Made surplus to requirements and dismissed means without work.
